reason: NOT AN ITEM (drafter's judgment, reviewer did not rule -- reversible at batch review). 'For clarity, each Order Forecast shall itemize...' has a DOCUMENT as its grammatical subject, not a party, so it has no obligor; section 3.5 forbids importing one from another sentence. 'Itemize' is also absent from the 34-verb taxonomy. Read as a content specification elaborating the preceding PROVIDE obligation (E03-01) rather than a separate duty -- the opening 'For clarity' is the drafter signalling exactly that. CONSEQUENCE: the segment yields TWO obligations, not the three the reviewer's ruling assumed. || RULED 2026-08-22 (B3): EXCLUSION CONFIRMED, on the NON-PARTY-SUBJECT ground ALONE. The 'For clarity signals elaboration' rationale is STRUCK as superseded by §4.3.1 (F9): 'For clarity' is one of that rule's named restatement markers, but its step 1 asks whether every scored field would be identical, and here action and object differ -- so §4.3.1 classifies this as a DISTINCT obligation, not a restatement. The exclusion stands because the grammatical subject is a document, not a party. CLAUSE-COUNT CORRECTION CONFIRMED: this segment yields TWO obligation-bearing clauses, not the three the earlier eligibility ruling assumed. Logged as §21 R6's first NOT_ANNOTATABLE entry.

reason: Cross-reference/agreement-to-agree: the primary duty is qualified 'to the extent permitted by applicable law and as mutually agreed by the parties' -- its content is not readable at segment scope until a separate agreement exists. Excluded for consistency with C04-101, logged earlier on the same ground ('provided that additional terms... have been negotiated in good faith and mutually agreed upon'). Drafter's judgment: reviewer did not rule. Secondary problems noted but not the basis: 'share' has no 34-verb taxonomy match (nearest DISCLOSE/PROVIDE/TRANSFER, none clean); a compound 'will cooperate'; and two clauses whose subject is 'Such information', not a party. || RULED 2026-08-22 (B4): EXCLUSION CONFIRMED, and now citable to §2's AMENDED cross-reference rule (F6) rather than resting on drafter's judgment: a cross-reference excludes when a SCORED FIELD's value cannot be determined without resolving it. Here action and object_class cannot be fixed until the parties agree, so it passes the amended test. This retroactively grounds C04-101, excluded earlier on the identical basis. The secondary problems noted in the original reason ('share' has no clean taxonomy match, a compound 'will cooperate', 'Such information' as subject) remain not the basis.
segment_text: (e) Data Sharing. Life Technologies and Biocept have entered into this Agreement to, among other things, establish individual databases of results from the Tests performed, which databases will include patient information such as demographic, disease characterization, treatment and outcome information. To that end, to the extent permitted by applicable law and as mutually agreed by the parties, where available each party will share all patient data, Test data and results, and corresponding tissue data with the other party, as well as any follow up or outcome data that may become available or provided by the physician or patient for Tests performed and will cooperate in good faith with the other party to agree upon procedures for sharing such information. Such information may be used only for longitudinal reporting, outcomes correlation and related research, shall be handled in accordance with all applicable Laws, including, without limitation, HIPAA, and applicable institutional review board guidelines, and shall not be used for the purpose of obtaining information about the other party's clients or customers. To the extent feasible, all such information will be properly de-identified.
